newsitem.title: USA: Gypsy moth found in new areas of Ohio, W.Virginia.
newsitem.headline: Gypsy moth found in new areas of Ohio, W.Virginia.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said Wednesday it added several counties in Ohio and West Virginia to a quarantine list of gypsy moth infestations.

In a notice published in the Federal Register, the agency's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service said it added Belmont, Coshocton, Harrison, Holmes, Monroe, and Tuscarawas Counties in Ohio to the quarantine list. The agency said it also added Doddridge, Harrison, Lewis, Tyler, and Upshur Counties in West Virginia.
The action restricts interstate movement to prevent the spread of the pest.
The gypsy moth, known to scientists as Lymantria dispar (Linnaeus), is a destructive pest of forest and shade trees.
